text:
carlos: FYI escalated customer on Vercel Edge. Browser requests to our hosted API are blocked by preflight only when their app is bundled with es-module-shims. Works unbundled or when importing SDK from CDN. Repro + HAR attached. Preflight shows Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization but response lacks Access-Control-Allow-Headers. Ticket #54321.

carlos: Repro steps:
1) Next.js edge function (next@14), build with module-shim plugin
2) @redwood/inference-js 0.9.1-edge in browser
3) call client.generate(...) from page

carlos: Minimal fetch they ran:
```
await fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  mode: 'cors',
  credentials: 'omit',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
})
```

emma: thanks — can you paste the SDK bundle output and the exact SDK version? also any console error? :eyes:

carlos: SDK version 0.9.1-edge.
Console shows "Access to fetch at 'https://api...' from origin 'https://app.example' has been blocked by CORS: Request header field authorization is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Headers in preflight response." HAR attached.

sam: we’ve seen es-module-shims/polyfill patches that wrap request/headers serialization. Some polyfills call Request.clone() and that can drop non-standard header casing, which sometimes makes our edge auth middleware not match header keys. Not exactly a Vercel runtime bug but an interaction.

sam: quick try: can customer set header name to lowercase 'authorization' explicitly in the bundler step? or use a custom header 'x-rw-api-key' from the browser for now.

raj: we should patch the browser SDK to fall back to query param auth if Authorization header is absent in a CORS preflight environment. Low-risk hotfix: detect runtime (window exists and not a service worker) and send token as ?api_key=... only for browser calls.

carlos: customer tried proxying through a serverless function (server-side adds Authorization) and it succeeds -> confirms it's browser header problem.

emma: can eng produce a tiny edge-safe release that uses 'x-rw-auth' header and docs about why browsers sometimes strip Authorization with certain polyfills? Also add note about cookies vs header when using credentials.

sam: I'll draft a 0.9.2-edge with header fallback and a runtime detection flag. also add logging to detect when preflight lacks ACAH 'authorization' so we can surface in Sentry. assigning to eng-runtime.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-312 - edge CORS + module-shim header interaction (priority: P2)

carlos: customer ok with workaround for now, asked ETA. they also asked if this could cause billing double-charges when retries happen — they saw a retry loop in client after 401. :grimacing: 

sam: confirm: add idempotency on client request layer and stop automatic retry on 401 for browser flows. that'll avoid billing dupe. include that in hotfix.

emma: thanks team. @sam can you post the release PR link here when ready? I'll send the customer an ETA and the proxy workaround steps.

sam: will do — aiming for tomorrow morning UTC. thanks.
